pages.title: The poster shelf
pages.description: The book projects on my desk often include campaign material and advertising. These four works use that visual language to address financial access, institutional buyers and the circulation of images. I keep them together when thinking about type, persuasion and who a poster is addressing.

blocks.content: 4 works / Curated set

The book projects on my desk often include campaign material and advertising. These four works use that visual language to address financial access, institutional buyers and the circulation of images. I keep them together when thinking about type, persuasion and who a poster is addressing.

I keep these together because they treat words as part of the composition. SeizeJPGs and NakamotoFreedom make their statements immediately; MEME FACTORY allows the landscape to hold attention after the headline has registered. The Institutions Are Coming brings a different tone to the group.
4 in this set

blocks.content: 6 works / Curated set

Portraits were my way into digital art. I was already collecting photography books and found an unexpected connection between the carefully composed portrait and the deliberately crude avatar. This set follows that interest through borrowed characters, caricature and Ebrahim_Elmi’s Tears of the Desert.

This selection began with 6529Seizing and expanded as I encountered very different treatments of the face. Ebrahim_Elmi’s photograph sits alongside work by OSF, Arsonic, Tyronejkd and Botto. The comparison is editorial; it makes no claim that these artists share a method or intention.

pages.title: Three Blitmaps
pages.description: My interest in Blitmap comes from working at the other end of the scale: large printed pages assembled from many small decisions. These original works use a 32 × 32 grid, where a single pixel can change an edge or an expression.

blocks.content: 3 works / Curated set

My interest in Blitmap comes from working at the other end of the scale: large printed pages assembled from many small decisions. These original works use a 32 × 32 grid, where a single pixel can change an edge or an expression.

I chose Rose, Psychic and Jupiter for their different treatment of familiar subjects. I keep the enlarged pixel edges visible rather than smoothing them for the screen. The original collection is public domain; the work records here retain the onchain creator names.
3 in this set

pages.title: Notebook.
pages.description: Working notes on the selection. I write these to remember what held my attention and what changed when I put one work beside another.

blocks.content: Looking, pairing, revising
Working notes on the selection. I write these to remember what held my attention and what changed when I put one work beside another.
12 September 2026

blocks.title: Freedom to Explore by Cath Simard

blocks.content: I selected Freedom to Explore as a link between the landscapes and posters on this wall. Its statement about freedom is explicit, but the immersive setting gives it a different weight from the emphatic lettering of SeizeJPGs.
That relationship is easy to miss in a thumbnail. The figure establishes the scale of the cavern; at a larger size, the political statement becomes one element within a much more expansive image.
8 September 2026

blocks.title: MEME FACTORY by Grant Riven Yun

blocks.text: MEME FACTORY and the poster format

blocks.content: MEME FACTORY combines the emphatic language of a poster with an unusually restrained industrial landscape. The power lines, trees and chimney bands reward attention after the headline has registered.
I’ve paired it with Freedom to Explore to compare their treatment of place. Both embed a statement in a landscape, but their use of depth, colour and typography produces very different encounters.
2 September 2026

blocks.text: Keeping the original file in view

blocks.content: A still image is useful when arranging a page, but it leaves out a defining part of an animated work. I keep the original records beside EXIT STRATEGY, rekt6529 and NO HUMAN INTERFACE so that the browsing format does not become a substitute for the work.

This also changes how I use the notebook. I can compare a printed proof of several stills, then return to the moving files before settling on a sequence. The final grouping needs to hold up in both situations.
26 August 2026

I added Rose, Psychic and Jupiter after trying a page of much smaller images. Enlarging the pixel grid made their different decisions about shape and colour easier to compare. I have kept the three at the same size.
The shelf is deliberately separate from the poster and portrait groups. I want the collection labels and creator names to remain clear even when the works share a page.

pages.title: About Mara.
pages.description: Book design, digital art and a growing printed index of both.

blocks.content: Bristol, UK
Book design, digital art and a growing printed index of both.

blocks.title: The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil by ACK
blocks.caption: ACK · The Memes #375

blocks.content: I’m an independent book designer based in Bristol. I work with small publishers and artists on photography books, exhibition catalogues and occasional pamphlets. My working week usually involves arranging images, discussing captions with an editor and making paper proofs before anything goes to press.

I came to digital art through the artists I was following, then stayed for the collecting communities. The early Memes particularly interested me because their poster language was familiar, while the arguments and the way the images circulated were new to me. This selection has since expanded to include photography, animation and work that borrows the conventions of portraiture.

The sets here reflect how I organise my own references. They change when I find a better pairing or return to something I had dismissed too quickly. Freedom to Explore and The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil sit outside those groups for now; both are works I want to spend more time with before deciding where they belong.
